title: Twice the Height? Free Fall Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A mango drops from a branch, a coin slips off a table, a drop leaves a tap: one pull from the Earth runs all three. Diya sees a mango fall 4.9 m in one second. From twice the height, does it take two seconds? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn motion under gravity, or free fall.

A live motion notebook drops a mango from rest with a readout and a velocity-time graph linked to it, a slow-motion replay shows g and v as arrows, and ghost copies reveal the 1 : 3 : 5 rule. We derive v = gt, h = ½gt² and v² = 2gh step by step from the equations of motion, compare a 1 kg and a 5 kg stone, throw a ball straight up and see why the acceleration is still g at the top. Then a worked example, the exam trap about the sign of g, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A mango, a coin, a drop: one pull
0:27 What is free fall? g = 9.8 m/s² down
0:54 Live sim: drop from rest, slow-mo replay, 1 : 3 : 5
1:37 The formulas: v = gt, h = ½gt², v² = 2gh
2:18 Heavy vs light stone + pause and think
2:48 Thrown straight up: time up = time down
3:39 Worked example: Diya's mango from twice the height
4:07 Exam trap: the sign of g
4:30 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:11 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Position-Time Graphs. The mango's fall draws a curve on a graph. What does its shape tell you?
